code_name: Eloy, AZ Code of Ordinances, Chapter 21 Zoning (Article II Zoning Districts; Article III Supplemental Use Standards; Article IV General Development Regulations; Article IX Definitions)
edition: American Legal Publishing online code 'latest' as of 2026-10-16; use tables show Ord. 18-880 (7-23-2018), amd. Ord. 21-904 (2021), Ord. 21-911 (2021), Ord. 24-981 (10-14-2024, eff. 11-14-2024)
caveats: Code library blocks plain HTTP/WebFetch (403); text was read through a browser session. American Legal states the online code may not reflect the most current legislation; confirm with Eloy Community Development before relying on it.

District purposes are paraphrased from the city zoning GIS layer (https://services7.arcgis.com/VfOwt1fngp5cVBlk/arcgis/rest/services/EloyZoning_view_Public/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=Zoning,ShortDescription,LongDescription&returnDistinctValues=true&returnGeometry=false&f=json), whose text matches the code's district purpose paragraphs. The layer also contains RR-2.5 and OSC, which were not requested and are not documented here.

Data centers are NOT a listed use type anywhere in the use tables or the definitions (21-9-1). Under 21-2-5.3.G the Zoning Administrator classifies non-specified uses to the most similar listed use type; the outcome is not stated in code. Treat as 'not addressed'.

Explosives/chemical/hazardous manufacturing is not a separate use type. 'Manufacturing, heavy' (definition mentions storage of large volumes of highly flammable, toxic or explosive materials needed for the process; refining, metal rolling/drawing/extruding, asphalt batching, sawmills, packaging of fertilizer, paint, petroleum products, etc.) is permitted by right only in I-2. 'Manufacturing, light' definition includes machine, blacksmith, metalworking and welding shops and paint shops.

The ordinance has no stated PAD overlay specific to I-2 near I-10 and Sunland Gin Rd. The code only describes the generic PAD overlay (21-2-7.2 to 21-2-7.5). A site-specific PAD would be defined in its own approved PAD document/ordinance, which was not located. Note the code spells it 'Sunland Gin Road'.
Parking ratios, landscape rules and Article IV rules come from sections 21-4-1 and 21-4-2; only ratios relevant to industrial/residential/retail were read, not the full tables.

Residential setback columns (front/side/street side/rear) were read from a flattened table; side vs street-side assignment for the larger-lot districts is inferred from column order and should be verified against the source table.

Community playfields/parks, community recreation center, country club, golf course (unlighted), library, public safety facility, religious assembly, minor utility facility
Vacation home rentals

Truck stop: permitted by right; bus terminal permitted; recycling center permitted

Building materials sales (indoor retail and outdoor/wholesale), wholesale, research laboratory, indoor self-storage, auctions (indoor), offices, nursery, auto repair (major and minor), animal hospital/kennel, major utility facility and service yard

standards.min_lot_size: Min lot width 100'; no minimum area listed
standards.setbacks: Front 30' (15' for street-facing parking); side 20' (0' if adjacent also zero); side adjacent to residential 75'; street side 15'; rear 20'; rear adjacent to residential 75'
standards.other: 20' landscaped buffer where abutting residential or community trail (21-4-2.4); outside storage must be fully screened by 100% opaque 6-8' wall; parking: heavy manufacturing 1/1,000 sq ft GFA + office 1/350, light 1/500 + office 1/350, distribution warehouse 1/2,000 sq ft + yard 1/5,000; industrial design guidelines 21-2-5.5.

districts.notes: Corridor rule 21-2-5.5.E: adult-oriented businesses, auto wrecking/salvage, outdoor heavy rental, landfills and non-chartered financial institutions are prohibited in I-2 adjacent to I-10, Frontier St, SR 87, Sunland Gin Rd, Toltec Rd, Sunshine Blvd and Battaglia Rd (so auto wrecking and landfill CUPs are unavailable there). Utility-scale solar siting (21-3-1.39) is limited to south of I-10, about 2,200 ft or more from the I-10 southern ROW, with a 11,744-acre citywide cap. Data centers: not addressed (not a listed use; Zoning Administrator would classify). Truck terminals: not a listed use except truck stop (P) and bus terminal (P). No specific 'PAD overlay' for I-2 near I-10/Sunland Gin Rd exists in the ordinance text.

districts.name: Mixed-Use

districts.notes: Industrial uses (manufacturing, warehousing, outdoor storage) are not listed for MU; building materials indoor retail is CUP only.

districts.name: Planned Area Development (overlay)
districts.purpose: Overlay district giving the city and applicant flexibility in applying development standards in exchange for more creative planning and design; approved through the rezone process.
permitted_uses: Uses are set by the underlying base district unless the PAD document expands or restricts them (21-2-7.4.A)

standards.min_lot_size: Minimum 40 acres under one ownership (waivable by Community Development Director for stated reasons)
standards.max_height: Per PAD approval; base district standards otherwise
standards.setbacks: Per PAD approval; may be more or less restrictive than the base district
standards.other: At least 15% of net acreage as open space (OSC and/or OSR); not more than 50% of that open space may be golf course use; City Council approves deviations.

districts.notes: The ordinance does not describe any specific 'PAD overlay' for I-2 near I-10 and Sunland Gin Rd; the actual allowed uses and standards would be in that site's approved PAD document, not found. Utility-scale solar rules (21-3-1.39) also refer to existing PADs and let them be amended to add solar as a permitted use.
